articles.title: Jordan steps up security in wake of church massacre
articles.description: Security was stepped up at malls, foreign embassies and other locations across Jordan on Saturday, the US embassy in Amman said, a day after a deadly assault on a church that authorities described as a terrorist attack by extremists. Eight people were killed and 40 were injured when gunmen opened fire for several minutes in broad daylight during a funeral at the Greek Orthodox church in Karak governorate, the head of Jordan's Public Security Directorate said. There was no immediate claim of responsibility. Such attacks are rare in Jordan, although authorities in the US-allied kingdom say they have repeatedly foiled plots by Islamist militants in recent years. Authorities said they were still searching for the attackers, adding it was too early to determine whether they had links to known groups inside or outside Jordan. "A massacre, a massacre in every sense of the word," said Tarek Ammarin at a hospital where the wounded were being treated. A relative of Ammarin's was injured in the attack. Police patrolled on Saturday outside the Hamoud church, about 120 kilometres southwest of the capital Amman. "This is a result of a terrorist ideology and blind extremism and we will not allow society to go down this path," Prime Minister Jafar Hassan said in a post on X. Jordan's King Abdullah, a US partner in the fight against militant Islamist groups, visited Karak hours after the attack and said the perpetrators would be punished "with an iron fist". Christians make up a minority of Jordan's population. The country is home to several biblical sites that attract Christian pilgrims from around the world. (Reuters) Edited by Tony Sabine
